core_obligations: Shrink the base so the dimension bound is global.
Invoke the finite-type plus base-change-commutation package for R^1.

proof_roadmap.step: Open neighbourhood reduction to affines with bounded fibres.
Cohomology-and-base-change bookkeeping concluding the fibre vanishing.

difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism f : X -> Y and a point y with dim X_y <= 1, the lemma shows H^1(X_y, O_{X_y}) = 0 if either R^1 f_* O_X = 0, or more generally if some base change g : Y' -> Y with y in the image kills R^1 of the pulled-back structure pushforward. The retained proof is written: shrink Y around y so all fibres have dimension <= 1 (Limits, lemma proper-top-cohomology... cited via the openness-of-bounded-fibre-dimension result Morphisms, lemma openness-bounded-dimension-fibres), note Y affine; then R^1 f_* O_X is a finite type quasi-coherent module whose formation commutes with arbitrary base change (the two cited Limits lemmas: finite type plus vanishing above the fibre dimension), so the fibre cohomology is the fibre of the sheaf, and the vanishing after base change through g with y in the image forces the stalk at y to vanish; the lemma follows immediately from these named inputs. Retained author proof at lines 20930-20940.

dedup.scope: Fibrewise H^1 vanishing detected after an arbitrary base change through the point.
